MEMBER AND FAMILY POLICIES

What you agree to when you join NGG

Version 2026.10 · Effective 10 October 2026. These apply to every member aged 10 to 17 and their parents or guardians. We record which version you agreed to and when.

Taking part and conduct

Members attend Saturday sessions at their centre, take part in their course, mentoring and club projects, and keep the Anchor Journal. Each member has a mentor who tracks their goals, attendance and Leadership Index scores.

  • Arrive on time, wear the ID card, and treat members, mentors and instructors with respect.
  • Repeated absence or lateness follows the club’s attendance policy, which can lead to a warning, suspension or loss of a place. The family is told at every stage.
  • Members upload their school results each session so mentors can plan support.

Safeguarding

Every mentor and instructor is vetted and trained before working with children. Adults never meet a member alone in private, and all online contact happens through the NGG platform or with a parent included. Concerns about a child’s safety are passed to the NGG safeguarding lead the same day, and to the family unless doing so would put the child at risk.

Emergency medical care

If a member is hurt or falls ill, we call the main contact first, then the second contact. If neither can be reached and care cannot wait, NGG staff may take the member to the nearest hospital or clinic and allow urgent treatment. We keep calling the family until we reach someone, and write up what happened.

Privacy and your data

NGG processes personal data under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. We collect only what we need to run the programme: the details in this form, the passport photo, attendance, scores, uploaded school results and mentor notes.

  • Who sees it: the member’s mentor, instructors and NGG admin. Not other families.
  • AI tools: we use AI to check photo quality and to draft study plans from results. A person reviews every plan before it is used.
  • Never sold: we never sell or rent personal data, and never share phone numbers or addresses publicly.
  • How long: while the member is active, then up to three years for records, after which we delete or anonymise it.
  • Your rights: you can ask to see, correct or delete your data, or withdraw a consent. You can also complain to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission.

Family updates

NGG works in partnership with families, so updates are part of membership. The main contact, and the second contact if given, receive:

  • Attendance alerts, including same-day notice of an absence.
  • Termly reports, Leadership Index scores and mentor evaluations.
  • Results analysis and the study plan agreed with the mentor.
  • Notices about sessions, events, fees and anything that affects the member’s place.
  • Invitations to parent meetings.

Updates go by SMS, email and WhatsApp to the contacts on file. This is a condition of membership. We do not send advertising from other organisations.

Photos and videos

NGG is a non-profit. Photos and videos from club activities are how we show supporters and partners the work, which keeps the club running. If you say yes, we may use them in reports, on our website and on social media.

  • We use first names only, and never show addresses, schools’ uniforms close-up, or phone numbers.
  • We never sell images or let others use them for advertising.
  • You can withdraw at any time. We stop new use straight away and remove images we control within 30 days.

This consent is a condition of membership. If you have a concern about a particular image, tell us and we will remove it. The ID card photo is separate and is only used on the card and in the member’s record.

Website feature

With your permission, we may show the member’s first name and work, such as a project, artwork or performance, on the NGG website. We never publish a surname, age or school together with a photo.

Off-site activities

Some activities happen away from the centre, such as visits, competitions and outreach. If you agree, members may take part under NGG supervision. We always send details to the family beforehand, and you can say no to any single trip.

Fees and payment

Nothing is paid when you apply. After acceptance we send a private invoice link by email and SMS for the membership fee and the first month’s commitment fee. The first month is charged only for the Saturdays left from the start date. Pay online with Paystack, or by bank transfer using the invoice number. Receipts are emailed.

Changing your choices

You can change your off-site answer and contact details at any time from the member portal or by contacting us. If we change these policies, we tell the family first and ask again where the law requires it.

Contact

Questions, data requests or concerns: email privacy@afrovanguard.org.ng, or speak to the coordinator at your centre on a Saturday.
